  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2"],
  "headline": "Intake established the service outcome, test requirement, and defaults for discovery.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a small Python HTTP service through which organisers create events with a seat count and people reserve seats; the usable outcome belongs in the repository's source checkout and becomes visible there at final return, while an isolated run's checkout remains at its snapshot until then. The request names no deployed target, so no deployment is assumed; a deployed outcome would exist only after release. Fact: the repository is empty, and this unattended intake implements nothing. Open interaction questions: discovery must first establish any existing runtime capabilities and relevant evidence, then resolve how organisers and reserving people are identified, how reservations share state across people, devices and sessions, how long that state lasts and what ends it, and what information is hidden from whom; these decisions block the corresponding API, storage, access-control and test designs. Recorded defaults if discovery finds no further requirements: anonymous HTTP callers with no organiser ownership or private data, shared persistent event and reservation state, and state retained indefinitely; these rule out identity-based permissions, confidentiality guarantees and automatic expiry. Discovery must also resolve reservation quantities, capacity enforcement and concurrent requests before finalising reservation behaviour and tests; absent further evidence, default to one seat per reservation, reject reservations exceeding capacity, and prevent concurrent overbooking. No team, workspace, channel, internal site, document, private repository, owner or ambiguous domain term is named as a source hint; discovery should treat any subsequently found lead as unverified and keep sensitive locators only in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/. S2 — Fact: include tests for the service; their results become visible when run in the delivered checkout."
}
